example (P : Prop) : P := by
  classical
  sorry

When I place cursor at the end of classical, it shows "No goals". Also pressing Enter there keeps "No goals" in the Infoview. Only when I move cursor to the beginning of sorry, the goal is correctly displayed.

Does it help to understand this proof as

example (P : Prop) : P := by
  classical
    sorry

classical is not a tactic, it's a block that wraps a tactic
that gives an explanation for why it is this way, but should it be this way?

Because it doesn't advance your proof state, it modulates how other tactics behave (which instances are available). This could be "fixed" if TacticM had a field for "are we using classical reasoning or not?" that other tactics or operations could then read. Then you could have a classical tactic that toggles the flag on and a constructivist tactic that turns the flag back off, if you want.
This could be used to fun effect where e.g. the itauto tactic is removed, and tauto merely reads that flag to decide which to dispatch to. :)
